question: Compare Datadog and New Relic on observability products

findings.evidence: Datadog states that its observability programme is delivered through a dedicated business unit.
findings.title: Datadog platform overview

findings.claim: New Relic describes its observability programme.
findings.evidence: New Relic states that its observability programme is organised around partner platforms.
findings.title: New Relic platform overview

findings.evidence: Both Datadog and New Relic report multi-year partnerships with major platform vendors.
findings.title: Partnership summary

findings.claim: An analyst note compares the two approaches.
findings.evidence: The note contrasts Datadog's in-house delivery with New Relic's partner-led model.
findings.title: Analyst note

findings.claim: Datadog discloses investment in observability capability.
findings.evidence: Datadog discloses continued investment in observability training and certification.
findings.title: Datadog investment disclosure

findings.claim: New Relic discloses investment in observability capability.
findings.evidence: New Relic discloses continued investment in observability delivery centres.
findings.title: New Relic investment disclosure

sections.heading: How Datadog organises observability
sections.body: Datadog runs observability through a dedicated unit. The competing approach is organised around partner platforms.

claims.text: Datadog delivers observability work through a dedicated business unit.
The competing vendor organises the same work around partner platforms.

verdicts.quote: Datadog states that its observability programme is delivered through a dedicated business unit.
New Relic states that its observability programme is organised around partner platforms.

notes: KNOWN DEFECT: the report never names New Relic, so a comparison answers half the question. expected_entity_coverage should read 0.5.
